newsitem.title: USA: Arch Comm to cut leverage, may sell assets.
newsitem.headline: Arch Comm to cut leverage, may sell assets.

text.p: Arch Communications Group Inc said it plans to put a higher priority on leverage reduction rather than subscriber unit growth in hopes of strengthening its balance sheet.
The paging company said leverage reduction efforts will include selling non-strategic assets and "slowing" of operating capital expenditures. It did not elaborate.
Arch said it expects to show positive free cash flow (EBITDA in excess of capital expenditures and debt service) within 24 months.

Arch said it expects its leverage multiple, defined as total debt divided by annualized current quarter EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization), to continue to drop as cash flow continues to increase and growth of debt slows and begins to decline.

Arch said it was shifting the operating focus, effective immediately, due partly to "new capital market expectations for many high-growth industries, including paging, that require lower debt-to-cash-flow ratios."
Arch said it expects to continue above average unit growth, but the growth will be secondary to leverage reduction.

Historically, Arch said, it has aggressively increased its subscriber base at a 40-percent annual rate, nearly twice the industry average. In 1996, alone, Arch added 815,000 new customers from internal growth, it said.
